A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Geo-R1 research despite the changed title and organization. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Geo-R1 experiments on cross-view pairing, GeoChain, IMAGEO, aerial geolocation and general VLM benchmarks, including training dynamics and appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds results on MP16-Reason, IM2GPS3K, GeoBench-VLM-CLS and an InternVL3 backbone, among other analyses.

M1.justification: The SFT data engine, cross-view GRPO procedure and detailed composite reward remain unchanged in v2 Appendices B-C. However, v2 Section 3 specifies binary -1/+1 rewards, whereas v1 and v2 Appendix C.2 assign -0.8 to incorrect choices and -1 to malformed answers. The PDFs do not resolve whether this is theoretical shorthand or an intended reward change.

E1.justification: v2 adds MP16-Reason and IM2GPS3K geolocation evaluations and GeoBench-VLM-CLS aerial tasks covering classification, counting, spatial relations and environmental assessment. These substantially broaden the evaluated task requirements beyond the retained geolocation, GeoChain and general-capability evaluations.

E2.justification: IMAGEO-GSS gains GeoCLIP, GPT-4o and InternVL3-8B comparisons (v2 Tables 2 and 12). New benchmark comparisons include GLOBE, GeoReasoner, GeoChat, EarthDial and specialist geolocators such as Translocator and GeoDecoder (Table 3, Figure 6 and Table 11). These are reported comparisons, rather than citation additions alone.

E3.justification: v2 adds a second backbone condition using InternVL3-8B and an explicit thinking-enabled versus direct-answer inference comparison on IM2GPS3K (Section 5.5 and Table 11). The retained experiments preserve their stated training budgets, sample sizes, evaluation splits and completion limits.

E4.justification: New analyses examine the contribution of inference-time thinking (Table 11), portability across backbones (Section 5.5), and reasoning-trace vocabulary (Figure 8). Appendix M adds three illustrated cases, including a failure attributed to overthinking. These extend the retained training-stage comparisons, training diagnostics and geolocation error analyses.

E5.justification: The within-batch reward standard-deviation analysis is retained, moving from v1 Figure 10 to v2 Figure 13. Neither version reports repeated-run evaluation summaries, seed-based uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The existing model-confidence scatterplots are also retained.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial benchmark and analysis results, including IM2GPS3K city-threshold accuracy of 27.2% without thinking and 41.3% with thinking (Table 11). Most original results remain unchanged, including Geo-R1's 82.4% cross-view accuracy. Llama-3.2-11B's IMAGEO-GSS city accuracy changes from 0.240233 in v1 Table 8 to 0.140930 in v2 Table 12.

T1.justification: v2 introduces Theorem 3.1 and extensive derivations in Appendices D-E concerning invariant-feature learning, an entropy-based reasoning margin and an OOD generalization guarantee. These introduce substantive assumptions about nuisance independence, geometric identifiability and causal invariance. v1 contains the training and reward equations but lacks this theoretical framework.

C1.justification: v1 centers its contribution on a two-stage geospatial reasoning framework. v2 reframes Geo-R1 as an instance of a broader principle that indirect rewards suffice for transferable reasoning, claims theoretical support for learning view-invariant understanding, and emphasizes transfer across 25+ tasks and competition with task-specific specialists.

C2.justification: v2 interprets transfer as evidence that cross-view rewards induce inverse-projection logic, physical-law understanding and a universal geospatial parser. It also interprets vocabulary and second-backbone results as evidence of human-aligned concepts and architectural generality. Appendix M newly identifies overthinking among visually similar locations as a concrete failure condition.

D1.justification: The original implementation frameworks, hardware descriptions, hyperparameters and training prompts are retained in relocated appendices. v2 adds the case-study inference prompt but removes v1's explicit model-download link and dedicated reproducibility statement; the code-access link remains. This changes access documentation without establishing that resource availability changed.

R1.justification: v2 explicitly grounds its approach in Mall et al.'s cross-view alignment work and contrasts indirect rewards with GLOBE's task-direct reinforcement learning. It adds substantial specialist-geolocation and aerial-VLM literature while removing the standalone chain-of-thought related-work discussion. This materially changes the contribution's positioning.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and conclusion are extensively rewritten around indirect rewards. Detailed method sections move into Appendices A-C, a theoretical section precedes the condensed method, and the experimental narrative is reorganized. This is substantial rewriting and restructuring beyond the addition of scientific content.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column main-text layout, transposes Table 1, and adds a conceptual diagram, benchmark charts, comparison tables, a wordcloud and illustrated cases. The original overview moves from v1 Figure 2 to v2 Appendix Figure 11, while retained plots and tables are resized or relocated throughout the document.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, specialist comparisons, aerial tasks, a second backbone and the thinking ablation materially strengthen empirical support for transfer. However, v2 makes stronger central theoretical claims: Appendix D does not establish that maximizing predictive information eliminates nuisance information, and Appendix E.2 moves from training-domain fit to vanishing error across all geometries without establishing that implication. The empirical gains and these unsupported guarantees leave the net quality direction uncertain.
